auditor_value: a₂ = −7a₁ (block 2 accelerates 7 times as fast as block 1, in the opposite direction; a₃ = −a₁, a₄ = −3a₁)

findings.quote: Each extra movable pulley in the chain multiplies the effect on the far end, which is why block 2's acceleration comes out seven times point 1's.
findings.note: Vague: 'multiplies the effect' names no factor and the factors are 1, 3, 7, not a fixed multiple. The literal reason is that each movable pulley's string doubles that pulley's own motion and adds block 1's, so each level is twice the previous plus one.
findings.fix: Each movable pulley moves with the string above it, and the string over it doubles that motion when it is passed to the next level while block 1 adds its own; so the factors grow 1, 3, 7 (each one is twice the previous plus one), and block 2's acceleration comes out seven times block 1's.

question_defect: The served text asks for 'point 2' and 'point 1' while the figure description names blocks 1 and 2; the solution reads them as the same, which is the only sensible reading. The text also carries a part (a) with no part (b) served.
notes: All three constraint equations and the substitutions match mine exactly; a₃ = −a₁, a₄ = −3a₁, a₂ = −7a₁. The single common_mistakes entry is genuine (treating everything below P₁ as one body moving with P₂ does give |a₂| = |a₁|).
